confirmed_detail.quote: Double explosions at a Bolivian military barracks killing at least three, injuring dozens, and leaving fourteen missing — with a homicide investigation opened — raise immediate questions about whether the event was an accident, sabotage, or something else, in a country with a history of political instability.
confirmed_detail.j1_why: absent from INPUT — the topic summary reports only pyrotechnic explosions, casualties, 14 missing and an opened homicide investigation; nothing in the topic list or previous_coverage describes Bolivian political instability, and this imported background is used to support the accept.
confirmed_detail.j2_why: The INPUT's Bolivia topic states only that pyrotechnic material exploded in a barracks, killing at least three, injuring dozens, leaving 14 missing, and that a homicide investigation was opened. Nothing in the topics or previous_coverage describes Bolivia as having a history of political instability; that characterization is absent from INPUT and is load-bearing for the accept.

confirmed_detail.quote: The mission has advanced from the reported Putin meeting to direct engagement in Kyiv with compromise proposals on the table — a material progression in the diplomatic track beyond the previously covered Moscow session and merely expected onward travel.
confirmed_detail.j1_why: The INPUT topic summary for ct-2026-09-07-00 says the envoys 'met Putin in Moscow and were expected in Kyiv' — still expected, not arrived. No 'direct engagement in Kyiv' is reported anywhere in the INPUT; the prior package tp-2026-09-06-001 already carries both the Moscow meeting and the expectation of onward travel, so the sole stated new development does not exist in the INPUT.
confirmed_detail.j2_why: The INPUT topic ct-2026-09-07-00 says the envoys 'met Putin in Moscow and were expected in Kyiv' — the Kyiv leg is still only expected, exactly as in prior package tp-2026-09-06-001 ('the envoys expected to travel on to Kyiv'). No 'direct engagement in Kyiv' appears anywhere in the INPUT; the asserted progression is the sole basis given for the follow-up.

confirmed_detail.quote: German-language sources uniquely attribute the prior diplomatic stall to the US war with Iran and Russia's support for Iran, a geopolitical framing entirely absent from all other language groups.
confirmed_detail.j1_why: The Iran-stall framing is not absent from other language groups: article 9 (en, Dawn) 'Notes that peace efforts have stalled while the US is focused on its war with Iran', article 26 (en, Responsible Statecraft) says diplomacy 'stalled when the US war with Iran began', and article 28 (en, Ukrinform) says the Geneva round 'was postponed after the US-Iran war began'.
confirmed_detail.j2_why: The stall-because-of-the-Iran-war framing is present in three English-language analyses: article_index 9 (Dawn, en) 'Notes that peace efforts have stalled while the US is focused on its war with Iran'; article_index 26 (Responsible Statecraft, en) 'after diplomacy stalled when the US war with Iran began'; article_index 28 (Ukrinform, en) 'the previous Geneva trilateral round was postponed after the US-Iran war began'. Only the 'Russia supporting Iran' detail is German-only.

confirmed_detail.quote: The Russian-language source uniquely reports that Washington specifically asked Kyiv to refrain from drone strikes on Russian energy infrastructure and cites Ukrainian intelligence chief Budanov's prediction of resumed trilateral talks in September, details not surfaced in any other language group.
confirmed_detail.j1_why: Article 21 gives Kirill Budanov the role 'Head of the Ukrainian Presidential Office', not intelligence chief; the title is imported from outside the input. (The drone/energy-infrastructure half of the sentence is correctly grounded in article 21.)
confirmed_detail.j2_why: article_index 21 identifies Kirill Budanov's role as 'Head of the Ukrainian Presidential Office'; the title 'Ukrainian intelligence chief' appears nowhere in the INPUT, and the analysis records him as not ruling out resumed trilateral talks rather than predicting them.

confirmed_detail.quote: Within English-language coverage the regional cluster split is stark: China's CGTN relays the visit only through unnamed TASS sourcing and Kremlin non-confirmation, quoting no Ukrainian officials and no casualties, while UK-, US-, Ukraine-, and Qatar-based outlets quote Zelensky directly and report deaths in Kamianske, Bucha, and Kyiv.
confirmed_detail.j1_why: The corpus has two CGTN items. Article 6 (en, China, CGTN) is a substantive report on the talks that quotes Volodymyr Zelenskyy announcing Ukraine's readiness to refrain from strikes on Moscow, alongside Ushakov and Peskov; only article 32 is the TASS-relay non-confirmation.
confirmed_detail.j2_why: CGTN appears twice in article_metadata (article_index 6 and 32). article_index 6 is substantive coverage of the three-hour Moscow talks quoting Ushakov, Peskov and Volodymyr Zelenskyy directly, so CGTN neither covers the visit 'only' via TASS relay nor quotes 'no Ukrainian officials'.

confirmed_detail.quote: South Asian language briefs (Nepali and Bengali) uniquely carry the report of a follow-up Trump phone call to both Putin and Zelensky and name regional Ukrainian officials' casualty counts, details absent from European- and Middle East-based coverage.
confirmed_detail.j1_why: Neither detail belongs to both briefs, and the second is not absent from European coverage: article 14 (en, United Kingdom, The Guardian) quotes Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, with casualty and damage details, and article 25 (fr, France, RFI) reports the Kamianske toll; the phone-call report appears only in article 22 (Nepali), and the regional-official casualty count only in article 24 (Bengali, Tkachenko).
confirmed_detail.j2_why: The Trump phone-call detail is in article_index 22 (Nepali) only, not in article_index 24 (Bengali); and named regional-official casualty counts are present in European coverage — article_index 14 (The Guardian, UK) quotes Oleksandr Hanzha of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration on deaths and damage, and article_index 27 (Tagesschau, de) reports five killed in the Dnipro steelworks strike.

confirmed_detail.quote: German- and French-language outlets (Der Spiegel, Tagesschau, RFI) alone report the war's Iranian domestic-economic dimension — the doubling of subsidized gasoline prices to 10,000 tomans, the lifting of the ban on government agencies using non-national messaging apps, and arrests over MEK flags — which no English-, Arabic-, Spanish-, Italian-, or Thai-language item mentions.
confirmed_detail.j1_why: The three named items appear only in RFI (article_index 15) and, for the fuel price alone, Der Spiegel (article_index 22). The three Tagesschau entries (article_index 16, 25, 28) cover IRGC/CENTCOM tanker claims, the maritime blockade tally and Tasnim's Kharg report, and contain none of the domestic-policy items attributed to them.
confirmed_detail.j2_why: None of the Tagesschau analyses (indices 16, 26 and 28) mentions gasoline prices, the messaging-platform ban or MEK arrests; the messaging-ban lifting and the MEK-flag arrests appear only in RFI (index 15) and the gasoline doubling only in RFI (15) and Der Spiegel (22).

confirmed_detail.quote: French-language coverage (RFI) uniquely reports Iranian domestic policy responses to the conflict — gasoline price doubling, lifting of social media bans for government agencies, and arrests of MEK sympathizers — dimensions entirely absent from all other language groups.
confirmed_detail.j1_why: article_index 22 (de, Germany, Der Spiegel) reports exactly the gasoline measure: government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohadscherani announcing the third-tier fuel price will double to 10,000 Toman from 8 September. The German language group therefore does report this dimension, so 'uniquely' and 'entirely absent from all other language groups' misrepresent the corpus.
confirmed_detail.j2_why: Der Spiegel (index 22, language de) reports the same doubling of the third-tier fuel price to 10,000 Toman from 8 September, quoting government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohadscherani, so the dimension is not absent from all other language groups.

confirmed_detail.quote: Arabic-language coverage (Al-Sumaria, Iraq) is the only reporting that carries the Iran-led 'resistance axis' counter-narrative — Quds Force commander Ismail Qaani declaring Hezbollah will remove Israel from the region and that Israel stands at the verge of collapse — while English, French, Spanish, German, and Italian coverage contain no Iranian official voice at all.

confirmed_detail.j2_why: article_index 9 (en, France 24) quotes Mohsen Rezaei, Head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, announcing an Iranian exclusion zone outside the Strait of Hormuz — an Iranian official voice in English-language coverage.

confirmed_detail.quote: German-language sources uniquely cover the joint condemnation of Israeli Gaza displacement plans by eight Muslim and Arab states and a German government minister's criticism, connecting the Lebanon escalation to broader regional Israeli territorial ambitions in a way no other language group does.

confirmed_detail.quote: Russian-language sources provide deep analytical skepticism citing Kremlin-linked sources that Putin will not compromise and detailing Russia's maximalist demands across multiple dimensions — neutrality, territory, army size, language rights, and elections — whereas English-language wire reports emphasize Witkoff's optimistic 'progress' language without equivalent independent verification.

The Russian-language entries are article_index 13 (hardening demands, Zaporizhzhia plant and Donbas as the two unresolved points) and 27 (a strike tally); neither enumerates language rights, elections or an army cap. confirmed_detail.j2_why: The enumerated maximalist demands (neutrality, keeping occupied territory, a cap on the Ukrainian army, Russian language rights, elections open to Russia-friendly parties) appear in article_index 20, whose metadata is language 'en', country 'Qatar', outlet 'Al Jazeera' — an English-language source, which is also the article that most strongly disputes the optimistic framing. The Russian-language articles (13, 27) describe hardening demands and the Kremlin-linked source but do not carry that five-dimension enumeration.

confirmed_detail.quote: Thai and Nepali wire reports emphasise Israel's 'strategic control' of the Ali al-Taher ridge and the ceasefire framework's failure to progress on withdrawal and disarmament, an analytical angle largely absent from English and Spanish coverage which focuses on the immediate human toll.

confirmed_detail.quote: The single quotes around 'by any means' present it as a verbatim quote, but no cited source provides this exact phrase. The closest verbatim is 'get them out — by sea, by air, by every way possible' from src-011, which is not cited for this sentence.

confirmed_detail.quote: Historians cited by src-010 (Rödder, Rother) and Katja Hoyer in src-027 argue the cordon sanitaire has failed and strengthened the AfD, while CDU figures in src-024 and src-033 insist cooperation remains impossible and Ann-Kristin Kölln in src-050 argues the firewall still holds.

confirmed_detail.j2_why: src-027 records Katja Hoyer as arguing that the AfD's breakthrough was driven by an upbeat campaign around Ulrich Siegmund and by mainstream parties' failure to offer a positive vision of change, so that migration alone no longer explains the party's rise. Nothing in src-027 attributes to her any claim about the cordon sanitaire or firewall having failed or strengthened the AfD; that argument belongs to Rödder in src-010.

confirmed_detail.quote: The IDF's World Central Kitchen investigation found that the seven aid workers were killed under a practice of "incrimination" establishing guilt by association, with Reserve Colonel Nochi Mendel saying the aid workers "were not innocent because they were connected to Hamas" and that he would do the same again [src-005].
confirmed_detail.j1_why: src-005 states that a Guardian investigation found the workers were targeted under an IDF practice of 'incrimination'; the IDF's own account in src-005 is that the strikes resulted from an erroneous assessment and failures to comply with orders, with no criminal offence warranting prosecution. The finding is attributed to the wrong party.

The INPUT contains no IDF investigation making the guilt-by-association finding.

confirmed_detail.quote: Iran States Missiles Struck US Aircraft Carrier as Hormuz Transits Fall to Record Lows
confirmed_detail.j1_why: The INPUT's traffic reporting says transits are at their lowest level since May (src-027) and gives Kpler figures of an average of ten cargo ships a day, two on Saturday and six on Sunday (src-023, src-027) and five to thirteen daily transits (src-002); no source in the INPUT describes the level as a record low.
confirmed_detail.j2_why: The INPUT's only characterisation of the transit level is src-027, which says mutual attacks 'have cut Strait of Hormuz shipping to its lowest level since May' with an average of ten cargo ships a day; no source in the INPUT describes transits as a record low. The same overstatement is repeated in the summary: 'Shipping data show Hormuz transits falling to record lows'.
